cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: A web server like Nginx handles HTTP itself: connections, TLS, static files, reverse proxying and load balancing. An application server runs application code. Node, Go, .NET and Rust include a production HTTP server; Python, Ruby and PHP need Gunicorn, Puma or PHP-FPM.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Put Nginx or a load balancer in front so app workers only see complete, ready requests. Nginx's event loop holds thousands of connections; a sync Gunicorn worker handles one request at a time. 502 means upstream broken or unreachable; 504 means too slow. Set Host, X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto.

questions.q: Requests taking about 40 seconds return 502, not 504. Why?
questions.a: Gunicorn's 30 second worker timeout kills the worker before Nginx's 60 second proxy_read_timeout. Inner timeouts should be shorter or equal.

questions.q: Uploads over 1 MB fail and app logs are empty. Why?
questions.a: Nginx client_max_body_size defaults to 1 MB and returns 413 before the app sees it.

questions.q: Force HTTPS causes a redirect loop. Why?
questions.a: TLS ends at Nginx so the app sees HTTP. Send X-Forwarded-Proto and make the app trust it.
